NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meeting videos are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 894 5223 3598, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 894 5223 3598, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 22, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Dev/Public Works Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RESOLUTION DECLARING OCTOBER 7, 2020 "CLEAN AIR DAY"

MAYOR SCHMITZ discussed the importance of clean air and managing air pollution,
especially in California with the current poor air quality due to recent wildfires.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL thanked the Coalition for Clean Air for starting this clean
air movement, and encouraged the community to try to do one thing on any day, especially
clean air day, to reduce pollution. She noted that our air basin has the worst quality air in the
nation, and that every little bit of effort helps.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF emphasized the importance of this day, especially in light of the
recent poor air quality due to the wildfires.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN echoed the importance of this cause.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN noted that the City of Rolling Hills Estates has defaulted
for 100% Clean Energy which is a large part of the carbon load that creates air pollution,
and thinks our City is pointed in the right direction.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE RESOLUTION 2468 DECLARING OCTOBER 7, 2020 “CLEAN
  AIR DAY”.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

5.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON UPDATE ON RECENT POWER OUTAGES

Government Relations Manager Vic Nol provided a summary of the outages that occurred
over Labor Day weekend, including the effect of the heat storm on equipment across the
entire territory, SCE’s efforts to restore power, lessons learned and next steps.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 22, 2020
 District Manager Ryan Robbins further explained efforts and failures that occurred over the
holiday weekend.

Distribution Engineer Louie Rangel explained phase balancing in detail, as a result of the
high demand over Labor Day Weekend.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL highlighted communication issues that residents
experienced during the recent power outages and inquired what communication
improvements will be made moving forward. Ryan Robbins encouraged residents to sign up
for outage e-notifications, recognized that their systems and communication resources over
Labor Day weekend were overwhelmed, and noted that they are working to improve the
communication process going forward.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL inquired specifically about the medical baseline customers
who require power for health reasons. Vic Nol explained that due to the scope of this
particular unplanned outage, additional notification to these customers was not possible but
is being considered for future events.

Ryan Robbins explained that changes are already being made within their systems, phase
balancing of the circuitry is occurring, and more work is being done to be proactive for future
events, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated that residents who experienced any loss of food or other
damage due to the power outage can file a claim with SCE.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN requested that as the City’s SCE representatives who
receive early notice of major events such as this, that they directly inform City staff who can
help get the message out to affected residents more quickly and efficiently through various
channels of communication.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN stated that his bill does not include an “outage group”
number, and that he contacted customer service who has not been able to assist him.

MAYOR SCHMITZ was pleased to see SCE recognize what lessons were learned from this
event.

Public comment was received from resident Loretta Britsch who asked via Zoom chat: “It is
my understanding that the issue was “Phase Imbalance.” From your graph, it appears that
the problem was becoming apparent as early as Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2020. We all knew
the weekend coming then was going to be extremely hot. So in retrospect, was there
anything that could have been done beginning Sept. 2, to avoid the power outage?” Ryan
Robbins explained that it is difficult to analyze the circuit during the event and there were
numerous variables causing many dynamic issues during a significant heat storm such as
this.

Resident Loretta Britsch also inquired via Zoom chat: “For the Rollingwood neighborhood,
what, if any, equipment failed as a result of the Phase Imbalance?” Ryan Robbins explained
that there was no equipment failure, however circuit breakers did open as a result of the
phase imbalance, and said that he would provide further information to the Council after
researching the area.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested to remove item 6E from the Consent Calendar.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 6A-D AND F-G AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 22, 2020
   AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63164 THROUGH 63216 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $181,738.48 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090320 THROUGH
  090620; 63098 (VOID); IN THE AMOUNT OF $103,899.95 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $285,638.43 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF AUGUST 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF AUGUST 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 8, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 15, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION

E.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 24, 2020

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the discussion in the Equestrian Committee
meeting minutes regarding the increase in manure rates and wondered if the City could re-
visit the rate increase, and specifically noted a typographical error in the minutes stating that
the City’s municipal code “does” allow the City to have more than one franchised hauler
(which should be corrected to “does not”). Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the
Waste Subcommittee has reconvened to look at this issue and plans to return to the City
Council with a report later this year.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the discussion within the minutes for Item C, in
which Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the City has not received a formal
request for trail riding operations and that no trail riding operations are currently taking place.
She further explained that staff is in the process of completing an agreement compliance
review and will continue to have open communication with the operator.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that Waste Management has postponed the
manure rate increase until January 2021 due to the pandemic, and echoed the efforts of the
Waste Subcommittee to look into some solutions.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE MINUTES AS AMENDED.

There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 22, 2020
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  RESPONSES TO THE 2019-20 CIVIL GRAND JURY REPORT ENTITLED “A DIET
  FOR LANDFILLS: CUTTING DOWN ON FOOD WASTE”

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that commercial food waste is taken to a recycling
facility in Orange, as required by our Waste Management contract, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER MITCHELL. COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL noted that we could improve our
efforts by including residential food waste, and suggested the Waste Subcommittee consider
this in their negotiations and discussions, which MAYOR SCHMITZ confirmed is already built
into the contract but has not yet been implemented.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF feels this is an important step for the City to take. She noted a typo
on the last page of the letter where “began” should be changed to “begun.”

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that many cities that are implementing the residential
food waste recycling are involved in partnerships with various entities such as farmer’s
markets, community gardens for composting etc., in response to MAYOR PRO TEM
ZUCKERMAN. MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN mentioned that some cities are allowing
small compost bags to be included in yard waste.

MAYOR SCHMITZ explained that the most recent waste contract negotiations were very
innovative and forward thinking, and considered upcoming legislation along with the City’s
desire to be responsible stewards of the environment.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL, TO
APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE EDITED RESPONSES TO THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF
  THE 2019-2020 CIVIL GRAND JURY REPORT ENTITLED “A DIET FOR
  LANDFILLS: CUTTING DOWN ON FOOD WASTE” AND AUTHORIZE THE
  MAYOR TO SIGN THE RESPONSE LETTER ON BEHALF OF THE CITY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
reporting that Los Angeles County continues to see a steady decline in the number of new
coronavirus cases. The County is currently in Tier 1 of the State’s four-tier reopening plan, and
has met the State’s metric threshold to move to Tier 2 but must continue to meet these metric
thresholds for two consecutive weeks before moving into the next tier.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided the following updates regarding upcoming City Events:
  • The virtual Hills Are Alive Race is currently open until October 12.
  • The City Celebration has been re-envisioned to include a birthday video featuring video
  clips from residents, businesses, Council and staff, as well as a 2020 time capsule.
  Items are currently being accepted at City Hall for the time capsule.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 22, 2020
   •  October 30 will be the second drive-in movie night featuring “The Nightmare Before
  Christmas”.
  •  There will be a Veteran’s Day ribbon-cutting ceremony for the recently completed
  Veteran’s Memorial at City Hall.
  •  The Mayor’s Breakfast Ride has also been revised and will take place in November,
  and will include a self-guided trail riding experience that highlights certain equestrian
  points of interest within the City and a video featuring the Mayor at each location.
  •  The Parade of Lights has also been re-imagined. The community will be invited to Ernie
  Howlett Park in early December to take a car tour of lit-up holiday displays. Santa Claus
  will also make a special appearance.
  •  In December there will be a holiday drive-in movie night, and staff is also working on a
  house decorating contest for the holidays as well.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported on actions made at the last California Air
Resources Board (CARB) meeting approving the three emission reduction plans for the
impacted Southern California cities, and that CARB would be considering approval of the
remaining emission reduction plans for the other AB 617 communities in California, at this
Thursday’s meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the South Bay Cities Council of Government
(SBCCOG) would be meeting this Thursday with guest speaker Dr. Thomas Parham,
president of Cal State University Dominguez Hills.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported on the meeting of the SBCCOG’s Senior Working
Group, where a stand-alone Department of Aging within Los Angeles County was discussed.
A program called Home Share South Bay was also discussed, matching seniors with those
in need of housing for a mutual assistance program.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF announced that the Senior Care Packages are now available to
all senior residents, and to sign up on the City’s website. Assistant City Manager Davis
reported that over 50 people have already signed up for the care packages.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported that California Contract Cities Association
(CCCA), through its Legislative Committee is working with legislators to propose more city-
friendly housing legislation to the State.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN reported that the Vector control meeting of September
was canceled, and that there have been no reported cases of West Nile Virus on the
Peninsula this year.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN also reported that he and COUNCIL MEMBER
ZERUNYAN met for a Nature Center Subcommittee meeting, and the Park and Activities
Commission and then the City Council can expect plans to review and comment on the plans
in the coming weeks.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on the monthly Peninsula Mayors meeting, where they
discussed scheduling a meeting with Southern California Edison to strengthen
communications with SCE, the City and the community.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, along with Assistant City Manager Davis, attended the
Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce’s Economic Development meeting. He
announced the Chamber’s Annual Legislative Forum on October 2, as well as the Top of the
Hill Open Air Marketplace taking place on October 3 and 4 from 10:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 22, 2020
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN also expressed frustration with the County in regards to its
one-size-fits-all approach to COVID-19, and strongly feels that a different approach is needed
to better fit the needs of the community given the low rates of infection on the Peninsula.

MAYOR SCHMITZ echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s frustration, and noted that
many of the Mayors on the Peninsula feel ignored by the County. She also reported that the
Mayors of the beach cities sent a letter to the County calling for reopening alternatives.

MAYOR SCHMITZ also reported on the reconvening of the Waste Subcommittee.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL brought up the community’s concerns about the closing of
the ice rink. MAYOR SCHMITZ noted that the rink is a private business owned by Stoltz
Management, who ultimately will decide on the fate of the rink.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Initiation of litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:57 pm MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular City
Council meeting on Tuesday, October 13, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular
meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Velveth Schmitz
City Clerk  Mayor

SEPTEMBER 22, 2020
